title: Exploring Plants: What Are Their Parts?
objectives: Identify the main parts of a plant (roots, stem, leaves, flower, fruit).
Describe the basic function of each plant part.
activities: "Plant Show and Tell": Begin by displaying various plant examples (e.g., a whole potted plant, a carrot (root), celery stalk (stem), different types of leaves, a flower, and a fruit like an apple). Ask students what they observe and what they already know about plants.

"Parts of a Plant Presentation": Use a large diagram of a plant and the real plant examples to introduce and name each main part: roots, stem, leaves, flower, and fruit. Briefly explain the primary function of each part in simple terms.

"Plant Dissection and Labeling": Divide students into small groups. Provide each group with a small, intact plant (e.g., a bean plant seedling, a small flower with its stem and roots attached) and a magnifying glass. Students will carefully observe the plant and try to identify the parts discussed. Hand out a worksheet with a blank plant diagram for students to label the parts they identify.
"Plant Part Match-Up (Optional)": If time allows, play a quick game where students match picture cards of plant parts to cards describing their functions.
materials: Variety of live plants (e.g., a potted plant, a carrot, a celery stalk, various leaves, a flower, a fruit like an apple).
Large diagram of a plant (poster or projection).
Optional: Picture cards of plant parts and their functions for a matching game.
assessment: Teacher observation of student participation and engagement during discussions and the hands-on activity.
Evaluation of completed plant diagrams on the worksheet for accurate labeling of plant parts.
Quick verbal check: Ask individual students to point to and name a specific plant part on a real plant or their drawing, and briefly state its function.
